html:
SMTO-EXE-0212 — This PDF doesn't allow that action

GUID: 11e22507-f9c6-55b0-9aa6-9fbb6803d82d
Slug: pdf-permission-denied
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • Either the PDF's own protection settings don't allow this action, or the Gateway computer won't let SMTO open or save the file. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the PDF is protected, save its owner (permissions) password as a PDF password in Parameter Store and mention it with @ in a new message. Editing a protected PDF, and sometimes copying its text, needs the owner password, not just the password that opens it.
  2. If you asked for page images, ask for them at 150 DPI or lower. Some protected PDFs only allow high-quality image output with full printing rights.
  3. If you were filling in a form, leave out fields that are marked read-only. Read-only fields are locked by the document and can't be filled.
  4. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to check that the Gateway's account can open the PDF and save in the target folder. The computer's own file permissions can also block SMTO from reading or saving.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the action and shows its result or a new file under Artifacts from this run.

If it still fails

  • Ask the document's owner for an unrestricted copy or the owner password, or select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't use other tools to strip the PDF's protection without the owner's permission.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The PDF action was refused by the document's permission flags or ownership (copying, printing or editing not allowed, or a read-only form field), or the Gateway's operating system denied file access.

What this means

  • PDF permission flags or ownership rejected extraction/printing/editing, a form field was read-only, or local file access raised PermissionError. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • PDF permission flags or ownership rejected extraction/printing/editing, a form field was read-only, or local file access raised PermissionError.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish document user/owner rights, form-field restrictions and OS access before choosing a remedy.

How to fix it

  • For encrypted PDFs, edits require the owner password and text, attachment, form and OCR reads require the EXTRACT permission when only the user password is supplied; rendering above 150 DPI also needs high-quality print permission, and read-only fields cannot be filled. Otherwise check that the Gateway's service account can read the source and write the destination folder. PDF restrictions are enforced, not bypassed.
  • Use a document and credential authorized for the requested operation, and verify local file access. Preserve enforced PDF restrictions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use an authorized document or its owner credential. PDF permission restrictions are enforced.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact requested operation is permitted by both document rights and authorized local file access.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
